subject: Display day of week on date axis

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Display day of week on date axis
parts:
One of my customers insists on displaying the day of week somehow on the X axis on the timeseries plot. The dow is particulary important to them. Is there an easy way to accomplish this on a plot like e.g. this:

dates <- as.Date(Sys.time()) - 10:1
values <- 5 + cumsum(rnorm(10));
mydata <- data.frame(dates, values);
ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) + geom_bar(stat="identity");

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Display day of week on date axis
parts:
On 5/25/2012 2:40 PM, Jeroen Ooms wrote:
> One of my customers insists on displaying the day of week somehow on the X
> axis on the timeseries plot. The dow is particulary important to them. Is
> there an easy way to accomplish this on a plot like e.g. this:
>
> dates<- as.Date(Sys.time()) - 10:1
> values<- 5 + cumsum(rnorm(10));
> mydata<- data.frame(dates, values);
> ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) + geom_bar(stat="identity");
>

Use the labels argument of scale_x_date; %a gives the abbreviated
weekday, $A, the full one:

ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") +
scale_x_date(labels=date_format("%a"))

or for an example of extremely verbose labels:

ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") +
scale_x_date(labels=date_format("%A, %B %d, %Y"))

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

Thanks, exactly what I was looking for. I think I am going to go with:

scale_x_date(labels=date_format("%A\n%B %d"));

To prevent labels from overlapping.

ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) +
 geom_bar(stat="identity") +
 scale_x_date(labels=date_format("%a"))

On 05/25/2012 05:40 PM, Jeroen Ooms wrote:
> One of my customers insists on displaying the day of week somehow on the X
> axis on the timeseries plot. The dow is particulary important to them. Is
> there an easy way to accomplish this on a plot like e.g. this:
>
> dates<- as.Date(Sys.time()) - 10:1
> values<- 5 + cumsum(rnorm(10));
> mydata<- data.frame(dates, values);
> ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) + geom_bar(stat="identity");
>

ggplot(aes(x=dates, y=values), data=mydata) + geom_bar(stat="identity")+
scale_x_date(labels=date_format("%A\n%b %d"));
-------------------------

Look at "?strftime" for all of the date format options. I added the "\n"
to split the date into to lines.

The following link helped me figure this out:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10576095/formatting-dates-with-scale-x-date-in-ggplot2

Jason
